September 15, 2026

Supreme Court blocks Trump mail-in ballot restrictions through the midterms

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

The Supreme Court declined to let the U.S. Postal Service enforce new mail-ballot requirements sought by President Trump, leaving in place a preliminary injunction issued by a federal judge in Massachusetts. The rule would have required states to provide lists of mail-ballot recipients and use USPS-approved envelopes with unique barcodes, allowing the agency to reject noncompliant ballots. The administration argued the measure would deter fraud, while challengers said it could block legitimate votes. Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented, and Justice Brett Kavanaugh said election officials lack time to implement the requirements before the 2026 elections.

Republican files eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of bypassing Congress in several U.S. military operations. Three articles concern the Iran war, alleging Hegseth began and continued hostilities without congressional authorization. Massie also cites the operation that captured Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela, military action in Yemen, extrajudicial strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats, civilian casualties and alleged efforts to suppress critics. The privileged resolution must be addressed by the House within two legislative days; House Democrats filed separate impeachment articles in April over the Iran war.

ICE agents beat two US citizen teenagers headed to enlist in the Marines

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Two U.S. citizen teenagers reportedly on their way to file enlistment paperwork with the Marines were pepper-sprayed and detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents for nearly eight hours before being released. According to Telemundo, the teens were detained after filming ICE agents arresting parents outside Santos Livas Elementary School in Alamo, Texas, and video shows an agent pulling one teenager from a vehicle and striking him while he was on the ground. One of the teens, Luis Ochoa, said he told agents he was a U.S. citizen and an agent replied, "I don't give a damn. Your parents can't help you now." The mother of one teenager said they are now reconsidering military service.

EPA repeals greenhouse gas limits on power plants

tags: climate, politics
sources: @groundnews

The Environmental Protection Agency is repealing Biden-era limits on greenhouse gas emissions from coal- and gas-fired power plants and proposing a separate rule aimed at restricting future federal regulation of power plant climate pollution. The EPA said eliminating the rule would save the industry more than $300 billion. Power plants produce about one-quarter of U.S. climate pollution, second only to transportation. Environmental groups have pledged legal challenges, while coal industry groups say the changes could support grid reliability and limit costs for electricity consumers.

Industry and political leaders split over Anthropic chief's call to slow AI development

tags: tech, politics
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay urging the AI industry to "pace the frontier," warning that self-improving systems could outrun their safeguards and that within six to 12 months a swarm of AI agents could seize enough internet-connected computers to cause hundreds of billions of dollars in damage; Anthropic committed to giving third-party evaluators permanent, employee-level access to its systems. Sam Altman said OpenAI would do the same and Elon Musk agreed, while Sen. Bernie Sanders called for a full pause on advanced AI and a ban on superintelligence, to be negotiated at an upcoming Trump-Xi summit. Former White House AI adviser David Sacks said the labs should slow down on their own but accused them of seeking regulatory capture, Palantir's Alex Karp cited foreign adversaries, and China's foreign ministry warned against fear-mongering. President Trump posted repeatedly on Truth Social defending AI and data centers, calling warnings a "sick conspiracy," and phoned into a live taping of the All-In podcast featuring Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; CNN reported White House officials are concerned he is downplaying the risks.

Congress opens investigation into Russian oligarch's funding of Don Jr's wedding

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Rep. Robert Garcia and the House Oversight Committee announced an investigation into reports that a Kremlin-linked Russian oligarch paid for parts of Donald Trump Jr's wedding to Bettina Anderson, which the couple confirmed receiving. Melania Trump said in a statement that she has never had a relationship with the man and played no role in organizing the event. Eric Trump and President Trump also said they do not know who he is. The president did not attend the wedding, citing the war in Iran.

Musk-funded voter site collects personal data and checks registration against its own list

tags: privacy, politics
sources: @carolinegleich, @total.hypocrisy

A website called VoteSafe is run by America PAC, Elon Musk's super PAC, and is neither a government nor a not-for-profit site. It collects names, dates of birth, home addresses, email addresses, cell numbers and location data, tracks page and link activity, and its privacy policy permits selling that information — including registration status and inferred "psychological trends, predisposition, attitudes, intelligence, and aptitude" — to business partners. Registration answers are checked against America PAC's own voter list rather than official state records, so users may be told they are registered when their county says otherwise. The PAC has spent more than $180,000 in a single week promoting the site on Facebook and Instagram; voters are being directed to vote.org instead.

Rising rates and fuel costs squeeze households as Costco rations motor oil

tags: markets, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Costco has begun rationing parts of its Kirkland Signature motor oil line and raising prices in response to the war with Iran, with a pack that once cost about $30 now costing about $58 and members limited to two units every seven days as supplies of premium base oils remain squeezed. Mortgage interest rates have risen above 7% and the 10-year Treasury note yield has surpassed 5%, its highest level since July 2007. Gas and diesel prices continue to rise.

Trump blames Biden for price increases and predicts oil will fall when Iran war ends

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

President Trump said in a Truth Social post that price increases throughout America were caused by Joe Biden and his administration rather than by Trump, adding that oil was higher under Biden than it is now and that his administration prevented Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. He said that with the temporary exception of oil, prices are coming down sharply. He predicted oil would "drop like a rock" as soon as the military conflict with Iran is over, which he said would not be long.

Trump shuts Kennedy Center after judge bars his name from the building

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge ruled that Trump's name cannot be placed on the Kennedy Center under any circumstances unless Congress approves it. Trump then announced on Truth Social that the building will close immediately and that reconstruction will be paused unless the Supreme Court allows his name to be added, in which case he said he would fund the rebuild and reopen it. Staff at the performing arts center are expected to be left without work.

McConnell returns to the Senate after weeks out of public view

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @hunteralexanderhowell

Senator Mitch McConnell was wheeled out of his Washington home on Monday afternoon and taken to the Senate after a day in which reporters gathered outside a shuttered house guarded by Capitol Police vehicles, with the Senate having convened at 3 p.m. He voted and gave brief remarks outside the Senate gallery, but reporters were prohibited from recording them. He appeared increasingly frail, with slowed speech, a dark spot visible on his hand, and footage showing him largely motionless in the vehicle. His condition has renewed debate over the age and health of sitting lawmakers.

Speaker Johnson pours cold water on Trump's promised $5,000 checks

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump has said Americans would receive $5,000 checks if Republicans win the midterms. House Speaker Mike Johnson, who would have to shepherd the legislation, said such a measure would take a long time and described the proposals as ideas. There is not currently enough support within the Republican caucus to pass the payments even if the party retains its House and Senate majorities.

National Voter Registration Day arrives amid mass voter roll purges

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @carolinegleich

September 15 was National Voter Registration Day, with organizers urging people to register or verify an existing registration, a process that takes about two minutes. Texas recently suspended 1.2 million voters — Democrats, Republicans and independents — without notifying them. Voters were also warned about fake websites collecting personal information, and reminded that moving, changing names, turning 18, becoming a citizen or sitting out elections can all require an update. Utah's registration deadline is October 23, with same-day in-person registration available afterward.

Former Trump aide and allies push to repeal the 19th Amendment

tags: politics
sources: @carolinegleich

John McEntee, a former Trump White House aide who ran the Presidential Personnel Office and later advised Project 2025, posted a video captioned "Sorry we want MALE only voting. The 19th might have to go," later saying he meant "male" as in men. Dale Partridge, a pastor in Prescott, Arizona, announced a book titled "19 Reasons to Repeal the 19th Amendment" and said he wants women's suffrage overturned within ten years. In August 2025 the Secretary of Defense shared a CNN segment featuring pastors who said they would support repealing the amendment, captioned "All of Christ for All of Life"; the Pentagon later said he does think women should have the right to vote. Utah women gained the vote in 1870, had it stripped by Congress in 1887 and took nine years to regain it, and women have voted at higher rates than men in every presidential election since 1984.

FBI signals it may investigate abortion pill manufacturer over mail use

tags: health, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

In Senate testimony, a senator pressed the FBI on Danco, the company responsible for most chemical abortion drugs made in the United States, saying it is based in the Cayman Islands with books unavailable to federal investigators and is coaching people on how to use the federal mail to evade state law. The senator asked whether the Bureau would investigate Danco and other offshore or foreign corporations using federal instrumentalities to violate state law. The bureau official replied that any use of the mail system in violation of a state law on the books is a federal crime that falls to the FBI, said he was not saying they were not already looking into it, and stated the agency is committed to that.

Anthropic says Claude was used to build targeting guides on US Navy personnel

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

Anthropic reported that its Claude model was used to build targeting handbooks covering U.S. Navy forces, including the names of sailors. In a separate case, a cell in Yemen used the model to develop guided-weapons software and returned to it after a failed rocket test.

Air commander says bases held bomb bodies they could not use in the Iran air war

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The U.S. air commander who ran the air campaign against Iran said bases held bomb bodies that could not be used in the operation, and explained the reasons behind the shortfall.

Watchdog report details damage from Iranian strikes on US tankers in Saudi Arabia

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Five U.S. KC-135 refuelling tankers were hit on the ground in Saudi Arabia during Iranian attacks. A new watchdog report sets out what the strikes actually damaged.

Iranian boats allegedly attempted to seize a US Navy drone in the Strait of Hormuz

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iranian boats allegedly tried to take a U.S. Navy drone in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident adds to confrontations between Iranian vessels and American assets in the waterway.

Some Air Force fighter pilots are flying about once a month

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A retired F-16 pilot says some Air Force fighter pilots may now be flying only about once a month. He said current official flying-hour figures are no longer publicly reported, making the decline harder to track.

ICE detains father of serving soldier while military parole application pending

tags: immigration, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A woman joined the Army and filed for military parole on behalf of her father. More than a year later, Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained him while the application was still pending.

Federal judge orders Army to revisit discharge over "condition, not a disability"

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army discharged a soldier on the grounds that the case involved a condition rather than a disability. A federal judge has ordered the service to review the case again, pointing to problems with how it was handled and with the medical record at the centre of it.

Trump revives Butler shooting claims as FBI director testifies

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

President Trump posted on Truth Social on the morning FBI Director Kash Patel testified before the Senate, saying the Biden-era FBI mishandled the investigation into the man who shot him in Butler, Pennsylvania. He wrote that by the time he took office on January 20, most of the information was missing, altered, corrupted or gone, that new information had just been found, and that the episode was a Democrat plot to remove him from the election. He said former director Christopher Wray should pay a price for his handling of the assassination attempt.

Congresswoman calls for public execution of Lindsay Clancy as pardon request stalls

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Rep. Nancy Mace of South Carolina, who previously called for the death penalty for Lindsay Clancy, said she should be publicly executed to make an example of her. President Trump said he has heard about attorney Kevin Reddington's request for a pardon but appeared unlikely to grant one, and a federal pardon would not affect her state case; he also did not indicate he would contact the Massachusetts prosecutor. The brother of the lone holdout juror told the New York Post that his brother looked at the case and made the call and that religion played no part, saying the choice "was good for some people but not good for other people." The next hearing date in the case is September 29, when major motions are expected.

Developer seeks land exchange that would open a road through Yosemite

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Kingsbarn Realty Capital, which owns an 83-acre property next to Yosemite National Park, is pursuing a land exchange that would connect its property to a road inside the park. The proposal under consideration involves roughly 1.1 acres of Yosemite, or an easement across the land, in exchange for property elsewhere, giving the company direct access to the park's main road system. Kingsbarn says it wants to develop the property for short-term tourism rentals. Critics warn the arrangement could set a precedent for protected public lands; no final decision has been made, and campaigners are calling for congressional oversight and public review.

House clerk could become a flashpoint in seating a new Congress

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The transfer of power in the House is not automatic: the clerk of the House of Representatives, a position meant to be nonpartisan, presides over the opening of a new Congress and runs the vote for Speaker, because neither the outgoing Speaker nor the incoming majority can oversee those proceedings. Nothing in the Constitution or statute explicitly prevents the sitting Speaker from removing the clerk and installing a replacement, a point legal scholars dispute, with many concluding it would be permissible. An acting clerk installed on those terms could decline to swear in members or hold the Speaker vote, pushing the dispute into the courts and delaying the seating of a new Congress.

Pentagon opens protected channel for UAP disclosures

tags: defence, government
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon has created a protected pathway allowing current and former personnel to disclose information about unidentified anomalous phenomena despite certain non-disclosure agreement restrictions. The pathway does not permit them to take the information directly to the public.

Intruder breaches Australian air base used by US Marines

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

An intruder allegedly breached RAAF Base Darwin, a facility used by U.S. Marines, assaulted security personnel and escaped in a stolen security vehicle. Police later pursued the vehicle and lost it.

Former AFSOC senior enlisted leader goes on trial

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The former top enlisted leader of Air Force Special Operations Command is now on trial. Prosecutors have begun detailing the allegations against him.

First results in from Hegseth's raised combat-arms fitness standard

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

More than 400 female Marines have now been tested under the new combat-arms physical fitness test scoring system introduced after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth raised the standard. The results of that testing have been released.

Ed Sheeran loses all four opening acts after removing Macklemore over Gaza remarks

tags: media
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy, @aaronparnas

Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran's tour after saying "Free Palestine" on stage, which Sheeran called hurtful to a lot of people while saying he wanted to remain apolitical. All four of Sheeran's opening acts — Lukas Graham, Finneas, Aaron Rowe and Bayoga — have since dropped out, leaving the Loop tour without a supporting act. Sheeran issued a statement saying he is appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine, that the suffering on both sides is a human tragedy, and that choosing not to speak publicly does not mean he is complicit. Critics argued his description of the situation as a conflict rather than a genocide is inaccurate, noted he has publicly backed Ukraine, and said touring revenue flows to billionaire venue owners who fund political campaigns.

Sailors told to remove air conditioners they bought for barracks without A/C

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Sailors living in a San Diego Navy barracks without air conditioning bought their own units during a heat wave. The Navy has now told them the units must be removed, citing reasons that complicate the dispute.

Roughly 90 USS Kearsarge sailors return from sea to find cars towed

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

About 90 sailors from the USS Kearsarge returned from several days at sea to discover their cars had been towed at Naval Station Norfolk. The stated reason for the towing added to the confusion.

Compilation argues 9/11 was a controlled demolition and false flag

tags: politics, media
sources: @ericmoutsos

A compilation of witness accounts, firefighter testimony and contemporaneous broadcasts is presented as evidence that explosions brought down the World Trade Center towers and Building 7. It includes Barry Jennings's account of an explosion on the eighth floor of Building 7, BBC and CNN reports of the Salomon Brothers building's collapse before it fell, and Wesley Clark's account of a Pentagon memo describing plans to take out seven countries in five years starting with Iraq and finishing with Iran.
